Funds will be used for the design of the project that includes the preparation of reports, plans and specifications needed to make improvements to the levee. The construction will address the following issues: raising the levee, installing relief wells, making drainage structure improvements, replacing conduits and pipes going into and along Peters Creek at several stations along the way, and replacing the drainage structure. Once the project is completed, it will provide the residents and rural area improved flood protection and increased safety.

program: SEARCH - Special Evaluation Assistance for Rural Communities and Households Grant (WEP)
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) SEARCH GRANTS WASTE ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment is to be used to complete a Preliminary Engineering Report surrounding the Citys wastewater system. The issues that have occurred with the system are at the lift station and are mainly caused by storm water inflow infiltration into the sewer mains. During these rain storm events, the backup pump becomes engaged, heats up and has been damaged. Infiltration is happening through cracks and holes in the sewer pipes, residential sump pumps, and damage from meat locker, grease and animal parts in system. This Preliminary Engineering Report will give the City information it needs to make informed decisions on what to do to get the wastewater system operating more efficiently and meet permit limits. This will benefit the community by having are safe and reliable sewer system.

This evaluation of their wastewater collection system and treatment facility is needed to determine the improvements necessary to get the wastewater facility to operate more efficiently and meet permit limits. Over the past couple years, their system has been experiencing excessive erosion on the lagoon cells dikes, which has allowed unauthorized discharges. The city needs to know what issues need to be addressed and select a path to follow, so that the wastewater system will function properly for years to come.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to focus on three schools located in frontier communities to deliver high-quality distant learning services. The three schools are Holy Family School, St. Joseph Catholic School, and Sacred Heart School, which together serve approximately 300 students. This project provides real-time, interactive telecommunication distance learning equipment, to deliver educational instruction and substance use prevention training to students living in Great Bend, Ellinwood, and Ness City, Kansas. This project will also help connect rural schools to support rural residents throughout Southwest Kansas.

funding_code: DISTANCE LEARNING- GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to build a telemedicine and distance learning network between 19 counties in Kansas. This project will improve our core infrastructure by expanding access points to internet / Wi-Fi connectivity and introduce state of the art dual-purpose equipment for distance education programs and behavior health services at our adult correctional facilities located in the rural areas of Winfield, Norton, Stockton, El Dorado, Oswego, Ellsworth, Learned and Lansing, Kansas. Through connections between the hub site and end-user sites, the project will provide 7,600 residents of the correctional facilities with the opportunity to access education programs, teacher resources, and secondary and post-secondary level instruction, while also expanding access to therapeutic services for residents in restrictive housing settings to engage in the full range of necessary treatment and support services to aide in their recovery process.

funding_code: TELEMEDICINE- GRANT

The system will serve approximately 144,000 residents in Morton, Stevens, Seward, Haskell, Grant, Finney, Kearney, and Stanton counties in Kansas; Baca County in Colorado; Cimarron and Texas counties in Oklahoma; Union County in New Mexico; and Dallam, Hansford, Ochiltree, and Sherman counties in Texas.

naics_industry_sector: Other Services
naics_national_industry: COMMERCIAL AND INDUSTRIAL MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT (EXCEPT AUTOMOTIVE AND ELECTRONIC) REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase and install heating and air conditioning systems and new lighting in the junior and senior high school facilities in Burlingame, Kansas. The current systems were installed in 1960 and are antiquated, inefficient and not environmentally friendly. Installation will include flat panel LED lights, to improve the quality of light as well as use resources more efficiently, and replacement of the entire heating and air conditioning system with a variant refrigerant flow zoning system. Due to the COVID-19 virus, it has come to light that older heating and air conditioning systems do not provide healthy air quality, nor do they help in preventing the spread of disease. Once the project is completed, the schools will provide students, staff and visitors with facilities that will provide a healthier and more conducive learning environment.

funding_code: CF 2019 DISASTER GRANT - TORNADOES FLOODS OTHER
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used toreplace portions of the existing gas supply line that runs along Kansas Highway 99 between the City of Wamego and Interstate 70. There will be construction of approximately 28,000 feet of new high pressure natural gas main along with tracer wire, 2 service connections, driveway restoration, gas main test stations and purging and abandonment of the existing natural gas main. The citys current gas system has been in place since 1960. Their current distribution system is in good working order and being properly maintained. There are several segments of the current system that are in good shape and no repairs or replacements will be made at this time. But there have been multiple leaks found in the gas feeder lines. These leaks have occurred due to corrosion. The corrosion is severe enough that it has occurred throughout the entire steel gas feeder line and is getting worse and will continue to get worse if nothing is done. To complete this project the City has acquired grant funds from the Kansas Department of Commerce in the form of a Community Development Block Grant in the amount of $600,000.00 along with a Rural Development Community Facility Disaster Grant in the amount of $303,300.00. When the project is completed the City will have a safe and reliable means of getting natural gas to rural residents of their community and the surrounding area.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to install new and repair existing water infrastructure. Funds will be used to drill six test wells, of which three will be developed into new production wells for the District. Funds will also help to install approximately one mile of transmission main to connect the new wells into the existing main of the Districts treatment plant, electrical controls and monitoring equipment. The District experienced a severe reduction in water levels in their six wells during the drought of 2018. In tracking the Districts well water levels, it was detected that the water was approximately 10-15 feet lower than normal conditions. One well was experiencing high levels of iron and manganese bacteria blocking the well screen and had to be shut down, leaving them with only five wells to supply the system. Water speed had to be reduced to keep wells from sucking air and causing cavitation and damage to the pumps. The decreased flow coming from the wells created operational issues at the treatment plant. The proposed project is needed to insure the system has adequate water supply for operating the treatment plant and for their customers during the extremely dry conditions in the future.

funding_code: DLT GRANTS - SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER - MEDICAL
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will help establish telehealth programs that connect vulnerable populations across four rural counties to vital services that address public health needs and the treatment of opioid, methamphetamine and substance use disorder. The project will use interactive equipment to connect county jails to critical nursing services through telemedicine technologies. Clients of the health departments will be able to access public health services remotely. Community corrections and juvenile services will be able to provide vital counseling, treatment and educational programs that address substance use disorder. The program will create regional access to public health that is not currently available due to geographical barriers and personnel shortages. Equipment will be installed in two jails, four county health departments and at the district location of community corrections and juvenile services. The project will improve outreach with public health and treatment services through professional consultation, medical diagnoses, medical treatment, and by providing essential public health programs.

Next to Nature Farm is a bee farm of 58 hives that produce honey and beeswax. They also grow fruit trees, which they use the harvested fruit to process and market preserved foods including jams, jellies, old-fashioned pickles and honey sticks. These items are sold at county fairs, festivals, holiday markets and other vendor events throughout the year. They also operate two metro-area farmers markets.

The city plans to replace 16,310 feet of pipe and increase the size of water lines to increase water pressure to the west part of the city, as well as installing and replacing 105 valves to minimize areas shut down due to repair leaks. A Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system will be installed for more reliable and consistent operation of the citys three wells. These improvements will improve the quality and quantity of the citys water.

The improvements are necessary to make the intersection safer for rural residents.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to complete a sanitary sewer evaluation survey (SSES) for the collection system, lift stations, and wastewater treatment facility. The city has had numerous sanitary sewer overflows from recent rains and is experiencing a large amount of inflow and infiltration associated with the overflows. To meet its monthly compliance with the Kansas Department of Health and Environment, improvements are needed at the sewer plant. Several of the components of the citys wastewater system require an abnormal amount of maintenance, and the city needs a feasibility study to fully understand the systems condition and plan for necessary improvements.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to evaluate the citys water distribution system. The citys water distribution system is in poor condition and is experiencing several line breaks causing significant water loss. The city needs a feasibility study to fully understand the systems condition and plan for necessary improvements. This will assist the patrons in developing a financially feasible project to correct the identified deficiencies of the system.
